editorial.brief: Grand Theft Auto VI is the story of the day, leading Wikipedia with 519,632 views while a first-play video on YouTube has 11,352,352. The second cross-feed item is Nvidia without Jensen Huang, with wire headlines and a Polymarket contract at 4% for his return. Hacker News spent its day on an unauthenticated Nginx remote code execution flaw, 1262 points.
editorial.cover_sub: Grand Theft Auto VI led Wikipedia by 1.3 times and turned up on Steam and YouTube in the same minute, which makes it the one subject the snapshot agrees on.
editorial.wiki_deck: Grand Theft Auto VI took 519,632 Wikipedia views, 1.3 times the runner-up, and appeared on Steam and YouTube as well. For once the feeds agree.
editorial.letter_headline: One video game, one departed chief executive
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is anxious about an Nginx remote code execution flaw, 1262 points. Lemmy mixes a grim 1995 history post with one titled Egg, Bluesky has an owl duet, and Mastodon would like to hide under blankets.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wires are on Nvidia without Jensen Huang and Anthropic's IPO orders at six times supply, while Brazil, Germany and India searched for Keyonte George.
editorial.markets_deck: Prediction markets split between corporate succession and the improbable: Anthropic's IPO-day valuation at 28%, Huang's return to Nvidia at 4%, and Walz and Roussel both at 0%.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaks at 1,221,105 players on Steam, with PUBG at 755,830 and Dota 2 at 728,011. On Twitch, caseoh_ has 99,615 viewers, ahead of TheBurntPeanut at 74,730 and KaiCenat at 43,745.
editorial.yt_note: The top video has 11,352,352 views, more than double the Avengers: Doomsday promotion at 5,276,826. A Christmas playlist, a Karol G lyric video and a Littlefoot trailer fill out the list.
editorial.closing_note: Gone by tomorrow's edition: the 4% on Huang returning, this hour's Twitch count for caseoh_, the owl duet, and quite possibly the 1.3 times margin Grand Theft Auto VI held over Ramayana: Part 1. Today's count of 25 earthquakes will be replaced by a new one.
wiki_paras: Grand Theft Auto VI drew 519,632 views on Wikipedia, the most of any article in the snapshot. Ramayana: Part 1 followed with 410,267, and Robert Pattinson was third with 337,514. The lead over second place is 1.3 times, a comfortable margin but not a rout.

The data offers an explanation. The game also appears on Steam and on YouTube in the same minute, where a video titled Playing GTA 6 For The First Time (Part 1) has 11,352,352 views. Three feeds pointing at one title is the pattern of a real event rather than a stray spike.

Below third place the list falls to about 150,000: Dancing with the Stars season 35 at 150,752, Suki Waterhouse at 146,794. The top of the table is a video game, Ramayana: Part 1 and an actor, and the game outread the actor by more than 182,000 views.
letter_paras: The snapshot reads as a two-story day with a loud centre. Grand Theft Auto VI appears on Wikipedia, Steam and YouTube at once, and the departure of Nvidia's chief executive runs through the wires, Polymarket and Wikipedia. Everything else is scattered: owls, blankets, a Thanksgiving aunt, a 6.1 earthquake near the Pacific-Antarctic Ridge.

Hacker News gave Unreal Tournament 2004 in the Browser 109 points, and Lemmy's fifth place went to a post titled Egg, with 699. Product Hunt's top three sit within 19 votes of each other. Cloudflare's busiest domain is google.com, followed by googleapis.com, which is the sort of order nobody reports.

A snapshot taken in one minute cannot be rearranged by hindsight. Nobody has had time to decide which story mattered, so the Nginx flaw, the owl duet and the Anthropic IPO orders sit on the same table, each at its real size. Taken daily, the pages become a record of proportion rather than of memory.
